items.title: Show HN: Voidleap Code – agentic IDE, own harness, swap models mid-conversation
items.why_it_matters: Voidleap Code is a new local, agentic IDE that lets you swap LLM models mid-conversation and edit the context directly. This is highly relevant because you can delegate simple boilerplate tasks to cheaper models like DeepSeek and swap to Claude only for complex architecture, mirroring the high-efficiency workflow you wanted to try. This week, download Voidleap, plug in your API keys, and try building your next AI-ingest feature by swapping between DeepSeek and Claude to see how much token cost you save.

items.title: Claude Code May–August 2026 weekly limits promotion
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic has introduced a promotional period from May to August 2026 that significantly increases the weekly usage limits for the Claude Code CLI. Since Claude Code is your primary tool for writing code, this means you can run much longer, more complex refactoring and building sessions without hitting a wall. This week, open your terminal and run a deep, multi-file refactoring session on AI-ingest's database integration without worrying about hitting your weekly limit.

items.title: Claude Code 2.1.234 continues your session automatically once usage limit resets
items.why_it_matters: The latest Claude Code update (version 2.1.234) now automatically resumes your active coding session once your usage limit resets, rather than failing and losing your context. This makes it much easier to run large, agentic code generation tasks overnight or during busy periods. This week, update your CLI by running `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` so your next major feature build can run uninterrupted.

items.title: Show HN: Maritime, a platform for running AI agents for $1 a month
items.why_it_matters: Maritime is a new platform built by MIT founders that lets you run isolated, persistent AI agents in microVMs for just $1 per agent per month. If you want to turn AI-ingest into a SaaS where every user gets their own background filtering agent with its own state and triggers, this solves the complex infrastructure headache for cheap. This week, sign up for Maritime and write a simple script to deploy a single background filtering agent to see how easily it handles persistent state.

items.title: fx :Tiny, open, native coding agent.
items.why_it_matters: `fx` is a new, lightweight, open-source native coding agent that runs directly in your terminal. It offers a fast, minimal alternative to heavier tools like Claude Code when you just need quick, localized code edits. This week, install `fx` via your terminal and ask it to write a quick helper function for your Supabase schema to see if it speeds up your micro-tasks.

items.title: Personetta – One YAML Persona for Cursor, Copilot, Claude, and Cline
items.why_it_matters: Personetta is a tool that lets you define a single YAML file to sync your custom system instructions and developer personas across Cursor, Copilot, Claude, and Cline. This ensures that whichever AI tool you are using always adheres to your specific Next.js and Supabase stack rules. This week, create a `personetta.yaml` file for AI-ingest containing your stack preferences and load it into your coding tools to keep your AI's output consistent.
